identity.industry: Capital Markets / Merchant Banking & SME Liquidity

summary.oneLiner: Gretex delivered resilient Q3FY26 results with 22.4% EBITDA margins despite seasonal lumpiness, backed by a robust pipeline of 20 active IPOs (6 Main Board) and a strategic pivot toward higher-value Main Board mandates to reduce inventory risk. Management guides for a sharp margin expansion to 40-45% PAT in Q4FY26 driven by scheduled listings, while the new AIF initiative diversifies revenue into pre-IPO investing without impacting dividend capacity.

one-line thesis: Gretex delivered resilient Q3FY26 results with 22.4% EBITDA margins despite seasonal lumpiness, backed by a robust pipeline of 20 active IPOs (6 Main Board) and a strategic pivot toward higher-value Main Board mandates to reduce inventory risk. Management guides for a sharp margin expansion to 40-45% PAT in Q4FY26 driven by scheduled listings, while the new AIF initiative diversifies revenue into pre-IPO investing without impacting dividend capacity.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 54.8cr (Q3), INR 144.8cr (9M); EBITDA: INR 12.3cr (Q3, 22.4% margin), INR 34.2cr (9M, 23.6% margin); PAT: INR 6.9cr (Q3, 12.5% margin), INR 20.7cr (9M, 14.3% margin); Order Book: 20 active IPOs (14 SME, 6 Main Board) + 26 Market Making mandates; Net Debt: Not explicitly disclosed, but strong cash flow implied by low capex and dividend intent; One-offs: INR 15 lakh SEBI penalty (final, no operational ban).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Lumpy quarter-to-quarter due to listing cycles; Margin: 40-45% PAT margin expected for full FY26 (driven by Q4 listings); Order Inflow: Steady pipeline with focus on Main Board; Capex: Minimal/no significant capex for tech upgrades in broking.
order book & pipeline: 20 Active IPOs (14 SME on NSE Emerge/BSE, 6 Main Board); 26 Market Making mandates (14 SME, 12 Institutional); Recent Listings: Flywing Simulator, M P K Steel, Munish Forge; In-Principle Approvals: SSG Furnishing, Vama Wovenfab, Shreyas Fabtech; DRHP Filed: Brandman Retail, Sureflo Techcon, Acetech E-Commerce.
segment / subsidiary detail: Merchant Banking: Core driver, 60+ historical issues (58 SME), fees resilient despite market volatility; Broking (Subsidiary): Preparing for own listing, low capex model; Market Making: 26 mandates, strategic shift to reduce SME inventory risk (5% compulsory investment) by pivoting to Main Board; AIF: New 50% JV in Bahutex Ventures (Cat II AIF), INR 100cr corpus, INR 2.5cr own commitment, focused on pre-IPO deals outside Gretex's direct mandates to avoid conflict.
growth verticals / optionality: Listing of subsidiary Gretex Share Broking Ltd; Scaling AIF book beyond initial INR 100cr; Capturing market share from smaller players exiting due to stricter SEBI net worth/track record norms; Conversion of 6 Main Board mandates which carry higher fee potential.
margins & cost dynamics: Margins are inherently lumpy (Q1/Q3 lower, Q2/Q4 higher) based on listing realization; Sustainable annual EBITDA margin ~20-22%; FY26 target 40-45% PAT margin; Cost structure disciplined with no major incremental headcount for Main Board (existing dual teams); No fee compression despite SME slowdown.
capex / expansion: Negligible; Technology upgrades in broking are routine/opex; No large-scale capex planned for FY26-27.
capital allocation: Dividend distribution expected to continue (AIF commitment of INR 2.5cr is immaterial); Reinvesting in pipeline execution; Strategic partnership in AIF for fee + carry opportunity.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory changes (SEBI norms); SME IPO market sentiment fatigue; Execution risk on Main Board conversions; Inventory risk in market making (being mitigated by shift to Main Board); Revenue lumpiness.
management quality / tone: Confident on FY26 being the 'best year'; Transparent about margin volatility being seasonal; Defensive on fees (no discounting despite market softness); Proactive on governance (welcomes stricter SEBI norms as industry moat).
non-obvious takeaways: Strategic pivot away from SME IPOs to Main Board is primarily driven by risk management (avoiding compulsory 5% market-making investment in volatile SME stocks) rather than just fee upside; The INR 15L SEBI penalty is confirmed as a closed chapter with no operational restrictions, removing an overhang.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SME IPO fatigue and subscription normalization | Nuvama Wealth | beneficiary | Med | Larger players may gain share if smaller merchant bankers exit due to capital constraints, though Nuvama is more wealth-focused. |
| Stricter SEBI net worth/track record norms for merchant bankers | Gretex Corporate Services | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary as management explicitly states these norms will limit competition and clean up the ecosystem, favoring established players like Gretex. |
| SME IPO fatigue and subscription normalization | Small Unlisted Merchant Bankers | loser | High | Likely to face exit or consolidation pressure due to inability to meet new SEBI capital/track record criteria. |

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
